Dear Dr. Mercer,

Thank you for seeing this 15-year-old high school student for an updated dermatologic and immunological assessment.

The patient's cutaneous troubles began at birth, presenting as universal bright red erythema accompanied by extensive peeling. Over the years, this has evolved into generalized eczematous eruptions characterized by relentless itching. The skin barrier has also been compromised by repeated bouts of superficial bacterial cutaneous infections requiring multiple courses of antibiotics. In addition, hair mount microscopy recently demonstrated distinctive bamboo-like hair shaft invaginations. Laboratory testing from last month demonstrated a strikingly raised total serum immunoglobulin E level.

Importantly, the absolute eosinophil count was entirely normal, and the neonatal course was free of hypernatremic fluid depletion. There has been no failure to gain weight or linear stunting; height and weight have consistently tracked along the 50th percentiles. Review of systems is negative for persistent loose bowel movements. On physical examination, while flexural lichenified plaques are prominent, there are no migratory double-edged polycyclic scaly rings. Cardiopulmonary auscultation is clear, and the patient has never suffered from reactive wheezing episodes, seasonal pollen allergies, hives, or bouts of deeper soft-tissue swelling.

The patient lives with both parents, enjoys playing the cello, and currently uses daily bland emollients and oral cetirizine. Family history is non-contributory.

I would greatly appreciate your evaluation and recommendations for ongoing management.

Warm regards,

Dr. Evelyn Reed
